unresolved: Obtain the complete Parkhill article and modern site chronology before accepting the synthesis’s Grid B hearth, pollen association, Folsom-like production and numerical age claims; the Hipwater Parkhill-phase record is a different locality.
Obtain Lepper/Tankersley chapters and exact outcrop or workshop records before creating Walhonding/Upper Mercer individual sites or dated procurement routes.
Obtain the complete Brown–Vierra Koster chapter and primary horizon dates. The eHRAF 8300–4900 BP coverage range is indexing context, not one uninterrupted local occupation.
Identify the correct archaeological Wall Ridge reference; do not silently replace Jill Duncan with an unrelated similarly named author.
Check full Jones dissertation stratigraphy, dating and alternative interpretations before assigning a numerical Carson-Conn-Short occupation interval.
For Coats-Hines-Litchy, review the original proposed age/association and later reevaluations together before presenting the full dispute; no early dated occupation added here.
Coordinates were not verified in the accessible sources. New records retain named fuzzy regional context and null geometry rather than precise site points.
Lambert metadata carries a 2025 volume/year and 2026 copyright note; retain repository citation year while leaving exact online chronology unresolved.
Full publisher text for several papers returned 403. Prior-source access notes are distinguished from new abstract/metadata review; no claim of reading inaccessible article bodies.
corrections: Krus 2019 dates Lawrenz Gun Club’s Mississippian phase, not the beginning of Midwest occupation around 13,000 cal BP. Its model intervals are kept separate from early Paleoindian evidence.

Belson already exists. Talbot 2021 is the relevant initial publication; the supplied attribution of its site details to Lothrop 2016 is not accepted as a direct site-dating reference. Nash 2024 still flags dating work pending.

Duncan 2020 is a Book review in History of Education Review, not a verified Wall Ridge excavation source. Exclude the asserted early-1300s Wall Ridge earthlodge and crop claims until the correct reference is obtained.

Jones 2018 is a doctoral dissertation, not a journal article. Its regional 13,200–10,000 yrs BP cannot become a calibrated Carson-Conn-Short site span; continuous residence remains an attributed interpretation.
Roosa is the missing author of the 1977 Parkhill paper (349–354). Parkhill is in Ontario, not a US site. Its 10,750–9,750 BP range is not relabelled cal BP or converted to BCE.
Brown and Vierra is a 1983 book chapter, reissued electronically in 2016; its supplied DOI is book-level. It appears in both RIS lists and is not two independent studies.
Tankersley and Lepper are book chapters, despite RIS JOUR tags; electronic metadata dates are not occupation ages.
235 Missouri/Iowa points are an artifact inventory, not 235 sites or people. Regional distribution does not establish continuous residence at any unnamed locus.
Legg’s existing predictive regional model is not an inventory of newly confirmed settlements or a proven migration route.

The Neolithic synthesis omits Woodland from its main sequence and overstates a universal prohibition on the term. Use region-specific Paleoindian, Archaic, Woodland, Mississippian, Oneota/Huber and Plains Village terminology where supported, without mapping them one-to-one onto Neolithic.
Cultivation, pottery and sedentism need not first appear together in Late Prehistoric societies. American Bottom antecedents extend into earlier regional periods.

Middle Grant Creek’s single-component early-seventeenth-century description cannot date Knoll Springs or all Langford/Huber occupations; no exact date, population, maize intensity or storage quantity inferred.
